medications.purpose: Reduce LDL‑C to target <1.8 mmol/L (or <1.4 mmol/L if very high risk) as first‑line therapy
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 2022 recommends high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 40 mg) as first‑line for heterozygous FH

medications.purpose: Add to maximally tolerated statin if LDL‑C target not achieved after 4–6 weeks
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 2022 advises adding ezetimibe 10 mg daily when LDL‑C remains ≥1.8 mmol/L on high‑intensity statin

medications.purpose: Further lower LDL‑C when target not met despite maximally tolerated statin + ezetimibe or when statin intolerance
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 2022 recommends PCSK9‑inhibitor (alirocumab) if LDL‑C ≥1.8 mmol/L after statin + ezetimibe

assumptions_warnings: Patient age, sex and pregnancy status not provided – assumed adult non‑pregnant; verify before prescribing statin or PCSK9‑i.
Liver function tests (ALT/AST) not available – statins contraindicated if >3× ULN; obtain results.
Renal function (eGFR) not provided – assume eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²; adjust if lower.
Current medication list not supplied – need to check for CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin) that may interact with atorvastatin; consider rosuvastatin if present.
Comorbidities (CVD, diabetes, CKD) and QRISK score not known – LDL‑C target may be <1.4 mmol/L; reassess after labs.
Allergy status unknown – confirm no hypersensitivity to PCSK9‑inhibitor components.
treatment_summary: Start high‑intensity atorvastatin 40 mg daily as first‑line therapy, add ezetimibe 10 mg daily if LDL‑C target is not reached after 4–6 weeks, and consider alirocumab 75 mg sub‑Q every 2 weeks if LDL‑C remains ≥1.8 mmol/L or if statin intolerance occurs. Monitor liver enzymes, CK, renal function and lipid profile, and review drug interactions once current medication list is available.
